name: Test specimens in chemistry, immunoassay and haematology (core laboratory)
summary: Community specimens that specimen processing has accessioned and sorted are loaded by laboratory assistants onto automated track lines and stand-alone haematology and urinalysis analysers. Middleware applies rules that release most results automatically; a registered technologist reviews the rest, orders repeats, dilutions and blood films, investigates delta check failures, cancels unsuitable specimens and confirms critical values. Results are released only while quality control is in control, so QC failures and analyser faults stop reporting and can force a look-back on earlier runs. Most elapsed time is queueing at the analyser input and in review queues during the evening arrival peak, plus instrument run time when nobody is working.

baseline.org_archetype: A large Canadian community laboratory company with regional hub laboratories running track-connected chemistry and immunoassay lines and haematology analysers with middleware autoverification.
baseline.notes: Covers the core laboratory from receipt of sorted racks to release of every core result on a requisition. Accessioning, daily QC, reporting and critical result calls are separate processes.

unit_of_work: one requisition with core laboratory tests (about five to six tests)
trigger: Specimen processing hands over accessioned, centrifuged and sorted tubes for a requisition to the core laboratory.
end_state: Every core laboratory test on the requisition is released to the LIS (autoverified or by a technologist), cancelled with a comment for recollection, or handed to the call desk as a critical value, and the tubes are in refrigerated storage.

volume.seasonality: Lower in July, August and late December; higher in January to March and September to November. Daily peak from late afternoon to midnight as courier routes arrive; Monday is the heaviest day.

evidence.note: Taken from the organisation file process map (cl-core-testing), which derives it from about 690,000 community requisitions a month; seasonality is the author's estimate.

roles.title: Medical laboratory technologist, chemistry and haematology

evidence.note: Cost from the organisation file (posted Brampton range and Job Bank Ontario high times 1.35). FTE on this process is the author's estimate: about two thirds of the 150 core technologists; the rest is QC, maintenance, calibration, insurance and trial testing, training and breaks not counted here.
Organisation file headcount 60; share on loading, unloading, storage, retrieval and slide handling estimated by the author.

Instrument middleware with autoverification and rerun rules
Automated chemistry and immunoassay analysers on track lines
Haematology analysers, slide makers and coagulation analysers
Quality control data management software (rules, peer comparison)

steps.name: Receive sorted specimen racks from processing
steps.description: A core laboratory assistant collects racks of centrifuged, accessioned tubes that specimen processing has sorted for chemistry, immunoassay, haematology and urinalysis, checks the rack count against the processing hand-off and stages them by priority (urgent first, then routine by arrival).

error.defect_description: A rack is staged at the wrong bench or left in processing.

next.condition: always

evidence.note: Hand-off between processing and core lab described in the organisation file process map; times are the author's estimate for a high-volume laboratory receiving most community specimens in the late afternoon and evening.

steps.name: Load tubes onto the track or analyser input
steps.description: The laboratory assistant places tubes into the track input module or directly onto stand-alone analysers (haematology, coagulation, urinalysis), clears tubes the reader rejects for an unreadable barcode or wrong orientation, and relabels or returns them to processing.

error.defect_description: A tube is rejected by the reader and set aside without follow-up.

next.condition: always

evidence.note: Author's estimate. Queue at the input reflects the evening arrival peak described for community laboratories that collect in the morning and test the same day (24-hour target in s_ag2017).

steps.name: Route tubes and download orders
steps.description: The track scans each barcode, queries the LIS through the middleware for the tests ordered, decaps the tube and sends it to the analysers that carry those assays; tubes for tests not on the line are diverted to an exit lane for manual benches.

error.defect_description: Order download fails for a tube, so it circulates or exits without testing.

next.condition: analysers in control and available
assay QC has failed, calibration is due or an analyser is down

evidence.note: Track and middleware routing is standard for automated core laboratories; the 3% share of requisitions caught by a QC failure or analyser fault is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for analyser and aspirate sample
steps.description: Routed tubes queue at each analyser until it aspirates them; chemistry and immunoassay run on track-connected modules while CBC and coagulation run on haematology analysers in parallel. Nobody works on the requisition during this queue.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: always

evidence.note: Analyser queue in the evening peak; author's estimate.

steps.name: Complete assays and apply autoverification rules
steps.description: After the assays finish (instrument run time of roughly 10 to 30 minutes for most chemistry and immunoassay tests), the middleware checks each result against instrument flags, serum indices, measuring range, delta checks, critical limits and QC status, releases passing results to the LIS and holds the rest or orders an automatic rerun, dilution or reflex test.

error.defect_description: An analytical error within QC limits passes the rules.

control.basis: ISO 15189:2012 clause 5.9.1 review of results before release; autoverification rules validated and approved by the medical director (CLSI AUTO10 practice); results released only while QC is accepted (Westgard multirule)

next.condition: rule orders an automatic rerun, dilution or reflex test
rules finished for this pass

evidence.note: Rule types and medical director approval from s_krasowski; QC rules from s_westgard; 3% of chemistry results flagged for repeat in s_deetz. The 10% per-requisition share (five to six tests plus reflex rules) is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run automatic rerun, dilution or reflex test
steps.description: The middleware sends the tube back to the analyser while it is still on the track for a repeat, an onboard dilution of an over-range result, or a reflex test set by an approved algorithm (for example free T4 after an abnormal TSH). Nobody touches the tube.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: repeat result returns to the rules

evidence.note: Dilution protocols and reflex rules in the middleware are described in s_krasowski; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Unload output racks and file tubes in refrigerated storage
steps.description: The laboratory assistant empties the track output or analyser trays, files tubes in dated storage racks in the walk-in refrigerator so they can be found for reruns and add-on tests, and leaves the result decisions to the middleware and technologists.

error.defect_description: A tube is filed in the wrong rack position and takes longer to retrieve.

control.basis: Specimen retention after examination for repeat or additional examinations (ISO 15189 post-examination handling of samples)

next.condition: every result on the requisition autoverified
one or more results held for technologist review
CBC flags meet the smear review criteria
a result exceeds a critical limit
a later QC failure puts this run inside the look-back window
a test is still pending at the end of the shift (tube not found or not tested)

evidence.note: Requisition-level shares are the author's estimates: test-level autoverification of about 90 to 95% in a mature community laboratory (99.5% in the academic lab in s_krasowski) gives roughly 60% of five-to-six-test requisitions with nothing held. Smear criteria met on about 8% of outpatient CBCs (CBC on about 55% of requisitions), well below the 26.7% median of mixed hospital populations in s_qp_smear. Critical share about 0.3% of requisitions from the organisation file. Storage practice is the author's description.

steps.name: Review held results in the middleware
steps.description: A technologist opens the middleware review queue, looks at each held result with its flags, serum indices, the patient's previous results and the other tests on the requisition, and decides to release it, rerun or dilute it, investigate a delta failure, cancel it as unsuitable, refer it, or treat it as a critical value.

error.defect_description: A result affected by interference or a pre-analytical problem is released.

control.basis: Medical Laboratory Technology Act, 1991: evaluation of the technical sufficiency of investigations and their results is within the registered MLT scope; ISO 15189:2012 clause 5.9.1

next.condition: result acceptable after review
manual repeat or dilution needed
delta check failure that needs investigation
specimen unsuitable (haemolysed, clotted, short, delayed separation)
unusual result needs a medical director or clinical biochemist
held result is a critical value

evidence.note: Review criteria from s_krasowski; MLT scope from s_cmlto_law. Branch shares are the author's estimate; the delta share is consistent with s_schifman, where only a minority of alerts changed what was reported.

steps.name: Retrieve tube and run a manual repeat or dilution
steps.description: The laboratory assistant prints or reads the retrieval list, finds the tube in the dated storage rack, and loads it for the repeat or a manual dilution the technologist specified; the repeat result returns to the technologist's review queue.

error.defect_description: Wrong tube retrieved or wrong dilution factor entered.

next.condition: repeat result back in review

evidence.note: Retrieval lists worked in batches through the shift; author's estimate.

steps.name: Investigate a delta check failure
steps.description: The technologist compares the result with the patient's earlier values and the other analytes, views the requisition image and label details, checks for a transfusion, treatment or known condition, and, if a mislabel is suspected, checks the collection site record before deciding.

error.defect_description: A mislabelled specimen is accepted as a true change.

control.basis: ISO 15189:2012 clause 5.9.1 review against previous results; laboratory delta check procedure

next.condition: change explained; release
specimen suspect; cancel and recollect
refer to medical director
repeat on the same tube first

evidence.note: In s_schifman 55.8% of alert episodes were reported unchanged and 3.0% not reported; median actions were clinical review 38.0% and retest 25.0%. Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Cancel the affected test with a comment and request recollection
steps.description: The technologist cancels or suppresses the unsuitable result in the LIS with a standard comment (for example haemolysed specimen, please recollect), releases the other results on the requisition and logs the specimen problem for the processing and collection teams.

error.defect_description: Wrong test cancelled or recollection note not sent.

control.basis: ISO 15189 sample acceptance and rejection criteria; OAML guideline treats haemolysed potassium as not meaningful

next.condition: remaining results released with the comment

evidence.note: Community specimen rejection rates of 0.2% and 0.9% (s_ag2017); haemolysed potassium rule (s_oaml). The roughly 1% of requisitions with one cancelled test is the author's estimate; it is higher than whole-specimen rejection because single tests are cancelled.

steps.name: Consult the medical director or clinical biochemist
steps.description: The technologist phones or messages the on-duty medical director or clinical biochemist about an unexpected or implausible result; the director reviews the case in the LIS and decides whether to release it with an interpretive comment, run further tests or reject the specimen.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: ISO 15189 laboratory director responsibility for interpretation and advisory services

next.condition: release, with or without a comment
further testing on the stored tube
reject and recollect

evidence.note: Daytime availability of medical staff and overnight testing drive the wait; author's estimate.

steps.name: Verify and release results manually
steps.description: The technologist releases the reviewed results to the LIS under their own login, adding any comment, which makes them available for reporting; the LIS records who released each result and when.

error.defect_description: Wrong comment or manual result entry error.

control.basis: Medical Laboratory Technology Act, 1991 scope of practice and laboratory licensing staff qualifications: results not autoverified are released by a registered MLT

next.condition: all results on the requisition released

evidence.note: MLT validates results (s_csmls) within the regulated scope (s_cmlto_law); time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare and stain a blood film
steps.description: For CBCs that meet the smear review criteria the slide maker-stainer prepares a film automatically; the laboratory assistant collects the stained slides, checks labels and film quality, and takes them to the morphology bench or loads them on the digital imaging analyser.

error.defect_description: Poor film quality needs a remake.

next.condition: always

evidence.note: Slide maker-stainers on haematology lines; author's estimate of handling time and wait.

steps.name: Review the blood film
steps.description: A technologist examines the film at the microscope or on the digital morphology screen, confirms or corrects the analyser differential, platelet estimate and red cell morphology, and decides to release, refer to a haematopathologist, request recollection (for example platelet clumping) or treat a finding as critical.

error.defect_description: Abnormal cells misclassified.

control.basis: Laboratory smear review criteria validated against consensus rules (ISO 15189 examination procedures)

next.condition: release with the manual differential
abnormal cells for pathologist review
specimen problem; recollect
critical finding such as malaria or a very low count

evidence.note: Manual review practice from s_qp_smear; times and branch shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Haematopathologist reviews the film
steps.description: The haematopathologist reviews the referred film and CBC history, writes an interpretive comment (for example suggesting further investigation for possible leukaemia) and returns the case to the technologist for release.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Laboratory haematology referral criteria for pathologist film review

next.condition: comment added; release

evidence.note: Films referred overnight are reviewed during the pathologist's day; author's estimate.

steps.name: Confirm a critical value
steps.description: The technologist checks specimen integrity (haemolysis, clots, delayed separation), looks for the same critical value in the past four months, repeats the test if the laboratory procedure asks for it, and decides whether the result meets the Level I criteria for an immediate call.

error.defect_description: A true critical is classed as recurrent or expected.

control.basis: OAML Guideline for Reporting Laboratory Test Results (CLP-025) Level I criteria; ISO 15189:2012 clause 5.9.1 critical intervals

next.condition: Level I critical that must be phoned now
recurrent within four months outside office hours, or not confirmed on repeat

evidence.note: Four-month recurrence rule and limits from s_oaml, which the company publishes (s_dyn_oaml). The 20% not phoned immediately is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Release the critical result and queue the phone notification
steps.description: The technologist releases the critical result, flags it in the LIS critical call list with the value and limits, and alerts the results call desk by the queue or a phone call so that a call attendant can reach the ordering clinician.

error.defect_description: Critical queued without clinician contact details.

control.basis: OAML guideline: Level I results called to clinicians 24 hours a day, 7 days a week

next.condition: critical result handed to the call desk

evidence.note: Hand-off to a call desk is the organisation file's assumption; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hold specimens after a QC failure or analyser fault
steps.description: When the QC software rejects a run under the multirule or an analyser goes down, the technologist suspends reporting and autoverification for the assay, pulls or redirects the affected tubes, and starts troubleshooting (reagent, calibration, maintenance).

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: CLSI C24 out-of-control procedure and Westgard multirule rejection: stop patient reporting until QC is acceptable

next.condition: always

evidence.note: Procedure from s_clp_c24 and s_westgard; MLTs review abnormal QC (s_csmls). Per-requisition touch spreads event-level troubleshooting over the held requisitions; author's estimate.

steps.name: Log the fault and decide on recovery or backup
steps.description: The charge technologist logs a service call or maintenance request in the maintenance log, a reagent stock request or an IT ticket for a middleware or interface fault, and decides whether to wait for recalibration and QC, move work to a backup analyser, or escalate an extended outage.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: recover or move to a backup analyser on site
extended outage needs a manager decision

evidence.note: Organisation file process map links this process to maintenance, replenishment and the IT service desk; author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve diversion or overtime for an extended outage
steps.description: The laboratory manager approves overtime, a call-in, or sending the backlog to a sister laboratory, and informs client services if turnaround will slip.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Laboratory downtime and business continuity procedure

next.condition: always

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Run on the backup analyser and release with manual review
steps.description: After QC is acceptable again, or on the backup analyser, the technologist reruns the held tubes and reviews every result before release because some autoverification rules are switched off during recovery.

error.defect_description: A result is released before QC acceptance is confirmed.

control.basis: CLSI C24: patient testing resumes only after QC meets acceptance criteria

next.condition: results released after recovery

evidence.note: Resumption rule from s_clp_c24; the wait covers recalibration, QC reruns or a vendor visit; author's estimate.

steps.name: Retest a stored specimen in a QC look-back
steps.description: After a QC failure is found and corrected, the laboratory assistant retrieves stored tubes run since the last acceptable QC and reruns them on the corrected analyser so the original and repeat values can be compared.

error.defect_description: Wrong tube retrieved.

control.basis: CLSI C24 and ISO 15189 quality control: evaluate patient results since the last acceptable QC

next.condition: always

evidence.note: Look-back practice from s_clp_c24; share of requisitions and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Evaluate look-back differences and authorise corrected results
steps.description: The charge technologist compares each repeat with the released value against the allowable difference set by the laboratory director, and for results outside it enters a corrected result and starts an amended report and a nonconformance record.

error.defect_description: A clinically significant difference is judged acceptable.

control.basis: CLSI C24: corrected reports and provider notification when differences exceed the laboratory director's limits

next.condition: difference within limits
difference exceeds limits; corrected result issued

evidence.note: Decision rule from s_clp_c24; 15% corrected is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Trace a missing or untested tube from the pending list
steps.description: The charge technologist works the end-of-shift pending list, searches the track, input rejects, storage and processing for the tube, and either reloads it or has the test cancelled for recollection.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: tube found and reloaded
tube not found or too old; cancel and recollect

evidence.note: Pending lists reviewed each shift; author's estimate.

exceptions.name: QC failure or analyser fault
exceptions.description: The assay's QC run is rejected or an analyser fails; reporting stops, the fault is logged, and tubes wait for recovery or a backup analyser with manual review of every result.

exceptions.name: QC look-back
exceptions.description: A QC failure detected after a run puts already released results inside the look-back window; stored tubes are retested and about one in seven gets a corrected result and amended report.

exceptions.name: Missing or untested tube
exceptions.description: A tube is not found on the track or in storage at the end of the shift and is traced from the pending list, reloaded or cancelled for recollection.

exceptions.name: Unsuitable specimen
exceptions.description: Haemolysis, clotting, short sample, delayed separation or a suspected mislabel leads to one test being cancelled with a recollection comment while the rest are released.

exceptions.name: Critical value
exceptions.description: A result exceeds a Level I limit; the technologist confirms it, checks the four-month recurrence rule and hands it to the results call desk.

exceptions.name: Blood film review
exceptions.description: CBC flags meet the smear review criteria; a film is made and reviewed by a technologist and, for abnormal cells, a haematopathologist.

pain_points.description: Most community specimens arrive between late afternoon and midnight, so tubes queue at the track input and held results queue for review; overnight staffing sets how much is released by morning.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from the morning collection and same-day courier pattern described in the organisation file.

pain_points.description: Delta check alerts take technologist time but most end with the result reported unchanged.

evidence.note: 55.8% of alert episodes reported without change.

pain_points.description: Blood film review is manual microscope work that queues behind the analysers and depends on experienced technologists; pathologist referrals wait for the day shift.

evidence.note: Manual review is triggered mainly by instrument flags.

pain_points.description: A QC failure stops reporting for the assay and can force retesting of every specimen since the last acceptable QC, with corrected reports for some.
Manual reruns need a person to find the tube in dated storage racks, which adds a batch wait to each repeat.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for lines without automated refrigerated stockyards.

sources.title: Autoverification in a core clinical chemistry laboratory at an academic medical center (Krasowski et al.)
sources.supports: Autoverification rose from 40% (2000) to 99.5% of tests (2013); rules use instrument flags, haemolysis/icterus/lipaemia indices, reference, measuring range and manual review limits, critical values, delta checks and dilution protocols; all rules approved by the medical director; billable tests per hour rose from 14.9 to 19.7 (2005 to 2010).

sources.title: Westgard Rules: multirule QC
sources.supports: Multirule QC: 1-2s warning rule; 1-3s, 2-2s, R-4s, 4-1s and 10x rejection rules; a run is rejected if any rejection rule is violated.

sources.title: The 7 best practices to recover from an out-of-control event
sources.supports: Steps based on CLSI C24: stop patient reporting and turn off autoverification for the failed assay, route samples to an instrument with acceptable QC, find and correct the cause, reanalyse patient samples since the last acceptable QC, issue corrected reports and notify providers when differences exceed limits set by the laboratory director.

sources.title: 2017 Annual Report, Section 3.07: Laboratory Services in the Health Sector
sources.publisher: Office of the Auditor General of Ontario
sources.supports: Community laboratories target routine blood and chemistry results within 24 hours of specimen pickup (about 75% of their testing); two providers met it for 94% and 99% of tests in 2016/17; community specimen rejection rates 0.9% and 0.2%; all licensed laboratories must follow the provincial quality management program of accreditation and proficiency testing; the model laboratory was one of the three largest community laboratories visited.

sources.title: Guideline for Reporting Laboratory Test Results (CLP-025), revised September 2009
sources.publisher: Ontario Association of Medical Laboratories (copy hosted by the model laboratory)
sources.supports: Level I critical values are phoned 24 hours a day, 7 days a week; Level II alerts are phoned or faxed 08:00 to 20:00; marked results recurrent within four months are communicated only in business hours; urgent results 6 to 12 hours after receipt; haemolysed potassium is not treated as a critical or alert value; critical and alert limits for chemistry and haematology.

sources.title: OAML alert reporting
sources.supports: The company publishes the OAML reporting guideline to clinicians as its alert reporting protocol.

sources.title: New Q-Probes report: peripheral blood smear review

assumptions: Instrument run time and analyser queues are modelled as waiting with zero hands-on time (steps s04 to s06); event-level troubleshooting time is spread across the held requisitions as a fraction of a minute each.

Requisition-level autoverification is set at about 60% (nothing held). Test-level rates of 90 to 95% are assumed for a community laboratory in 2019-2022; the published 99.5% is from one academic chemistry laboratory and excludes haematology.
The qc_record, lis_change and competency_record inputs from the process map are enabling inputs, not case triggers, so they carry a share of 0 in interfaces.triggered_by.
Maintenance requests, stock requisitions and IT tickets are attached to the analyser fault outcome because they arise per analyser event, not per requisition.
Critical values are about 0.3% of core requisitions; the remainder of the organisation file's 2,500 critical calls a month come from microbiology and the reference laboratory.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (hourly wage times 1.35).

Organisation file check: about 640,000 requisitions of five to six tests a month (about 42 million tests a year) with 210 core laboratory staff is roughly 200,000 tests per person a year, about twice the 90th percentile (105,081) for the highest-volume laboratories in the 2004 Q-Probes study. Either the core headcount is low or the test count includes many low-effort analytes; the stated FTE here stay within the organisation file headcount.
The lab_ops_director role has no per-requisition step; its 0.2 FTE stands for turnaround and staffing oversight.
